text: Language Reference Language Shapes Rectangle / Box A step in the process or a screen in the flow. Use Case: Each screen in your React Native app (Home, Activity Feed, Bonding, Profile) would be a rectangle. Diamond A decision point (yes/no, sign in/out, success/fail). Use Case: If the user is new, do they see onboarding → yes/no? If yes, arrow flows to Onboarding screen; if no, arrow flows to Home screen. Arrows Flow or transition from one step/screen to the next. Use Case: For “User taps ‘Join Activity’,” you’d draw an arrow from “Activity Feed” to “Join Confirmation” screen. Circle or Ellipse Start/end points. Use Case: A circle labeled “App Launch” at the beginning, or “End” at the conclusion, though you might omit an explicit “End” if the flow is cyclical. Labels / Notes Meaning: Additional clarifications or conditions. Use Case: If a transition is conditional (“User has location sharing ON → Show local events”), you might annotate that next to the arrow. Color Blue rectangles = screens White rectangles = screen aggregation Purple rectangles = views within screens Yellow diamonds = decisions/conditionals Green shapes = external references or third-party interactions Bonding Overview “Bonding” is the process of establishing a trusted connection with another user. On initial import, you can instantly bond with people from your phone’s contact list if the system recognizes them (this is the one-time exception for bonding without meeting in person). After that initial import, you typically have to meet someone in real life to confirm or solidify the bond. Bonding States We b0nd recognizes four relationship states between users: Bonded Description: You have met in person (or used the initial contact import) and are now recognized as connections within the app. Privileges: Full profile view, direct DM with no restrictions, and the ability to see each other’s activities immediately. Pending Bond (needs a better name) Description: A user you’ve sent a bond request to but haven’t met in person, or they’ve sent a request to you. Privileges: Limited DM or partial profile view. You’re recognized as acquaintances but not fully “Bonded.” Friend-of-Friend Description: A second-degree connection—someone your bond is connected with, but you haven’t bonded or even chatted with them. Privileges: They can appear in your “Bonds Feed” if they co-post with your friend, or in your “Engage Feed” if they host an activity your friend is attending. You can’t directly see their entire profile unless they appear in the feed and you tap to expand a limited view. Unknown Description: Complete strangers to you—no direct or second-degree ties recognized by the system (or you simply haven’t encountered them yet). Privileges: They won’t appear in your feeds, and you can’t DM them. They’re basically invisible until you share a mutual friend or bond in person randomly. Bond Expiration / Dormancy If you haven’t interacted with a bond (no DMs, no co-attended events, etc.) in the last 90 days, that connection is marked as “dormant.” If 90 more days pass (i.e., 180 total days of no interaction), the bond is effectively undone. They revert to a previous state (like friend-of-friend or unknown). Why It Matters: Ensures that your “Bonded” list stays relevant and reflects true, active relationships. Pages High Level Client Structure This Architecture is Preliminary. Specifically, the structure of where screens are placed. A big question we have is where to put things for navigation purposes. For example, should chat be in the bottom navbar, or only accessible within a page? Instagram, for example, only allows chat to be accessed from home. Activities are like lighter Posts Activity Posts VS Profile Posts Profile Posts are Posts on your Profile which are part of your "Moodboard" They are relatively static. They cannot be commented on. They cannot be liked. They cannot be shared. Can only be updated by accessing "Edit Profile" on your Profile Page. Cannot be hidden from your Bonds or Users who your profile is shown to (in their recommendations) Are hidden from any blocked users Activity Posts are Posts that appear on your and other User's Home page, as well as in the Bonds (Friends) Feed They are relatively dynamic. They can be commented on. They can be reacted to (Double tap defaults to generic like). They can have likes hidden. They can be shared (only to common friends). They can be instantly replied to (DM quote -> flows into chat). They can be seen on a users profile by going to their "Activity" (Default is 14 days, see below for Privacy). They can be co-posted (tagged users are asked if they want to join on the post). They cannot be saved. They can be hidden. They can forward users to the poster's account. They can forward users to the tagged users accounts. They can be reported for abuse. Posting.svg Home Description The Home screen is the main app entrypoint and functions as a dashboard/synopsis of what WeB0nd has to offer you. The main focus of the Home screen is to quickly summarize what has been going on in WeB0nd as far as your bonds' activities, potential new bonds, and events. The second primary focus of the Home screen is to funnel users into the Feeds. By providing a synopsis of what is going on in each feed, users can navigate directly to the feeds. This page is fairly dynamic. For example, if you have recently attended an event, the first thing you will see usually be an option to rate the event. Architecture To the end of the above, different views and components are more useful than a static page. The state and particular attributes shown can be left to the concern of the engineers. Home.drawio.svg Profile The profile's design can be very subjective; honestly, getting many ideas of how it could look would be better than one fully polished idea. Nevertheless, some features are key: Moodboard A signature section on We b0nd profiles. Think of it like a curated gallery highlighting a user’s personal style or interests. I am thinking of two version for this: Static (MVP) Up to 6–9 photos arranged in a 2x3 or 3x3 grid. Similar to Bumble’s main photo carousel, but displayed in a grid. This would be clean and simple, easy to load, and visually appealing at a glance. Additionally, we can think of adding captions to photos when they are clicked. This click would load a full page view with more details on the photo, and, potentially, users can add the story of why they chose that particular picture. Dynamic (Post-MVP) Photos arranged in an artistic collage with varied sizing and alignment, possibly with a pinned “featured” image. The main idea would be to have the photos spread out and interlinked with other sections of the profile. Think about providing users to build out a couple of different layouts for their profile, from simple grid, to very intricate designs -> making their profiles truly feel like them Name and Bio This can range from minimal to more detailed, depending on user preference: Minimal (Instagram-Style)One line for username, one line for a short tagline—keeps the profile clean and concise. Extended (Location, Age, Pronouns, etc.)A full name field, custom handle, 1–2 lines for a summary, plus optional location, age, pronouns, etc.You might offer a toggle or “See More” expansion so users who want deeper info can reveal it. Badge Users can have a set of badges indicating special roles or statuses: Web0nd Employee: Displays a branded logo badge. Founding Member (within the first 10k sign-ups). Verified (for celebrities or notable figures). Moderator (review team members who accept users). Bonds Simple count of how many bonds the user has. Tapping on this leads to a secondary page showing: Common Bonds first, in their own category (clickable). Other Bonds (non-mutual) in a separate list, possibly non-clickable. Matchmaker When viewing someone else’s profile, you can act as a “matchmaker”: Displays a list of your bonds who might fit well with this person. Submitting a match request puts each party into the other’s “recommended users.” Attended Events Showcases real-world involvement in meetups, parties, or other gatherings. Possibly a simple list or visual badges for each event. Demonstrates how active the user is in the community. Highlight Reel A section for the user’s most noteworthy or proud moments, often drawn from Activity Posts or co-posts. Could function like a mini-gallery or “stories” feature. Visual implementation might vary (carousel, grid, etc.). Prompt Answers A Q&A segment where the user can answer brief, fun prompts: Helps break the ice and reveal more personality. Commonly found in dating apps, less so in typical social media—makes the profile stand out. Could be paired with the moodboard in a dynamic layout. Mutual Friend Indicators Displays how many (and which) friends you share with this user: Useful for trust-based contexts—“We have 4 mutual bonds.” Encourages conversation starters or shared experiences. Private Stats A section only the user can see, possibly including: Profile views or “visitors.” Bond request acceptance rate. Analytics/gamification elements (like badges for events attended, etc.). WeB0nd’s social media channels (Instagram, TikTok, etc.) Feeds We have 3 main feeds: Bonds (Friends) Feed Focus: Activities and updates from your direct bonds (friends) and second-degree connections (friends of friends). Primary Social Space: Where personal interactions (comments, DMs, group updates) unfold among people you’ve already connected with or have a close connection to. Bonding (People) Page Focus: Recommendations of new people you might want to bond with. Discovery Mechanism: Cyclical “bonding cycles” that refresh every 3–7 days with potential matches or suggestions. Engage (Activities & Events) Feed Focus: Social gatherings—both smaller friend-organized “activities” and larger “events.” Expansion of Network: Allows you to discover meetups hosted by friends of friends or organizations, even if you don’t personally know the host yet. Bonds (Friends) Feed Purpose and Content This is the main, go-to feed for seeing what your existing bonds (friends) have been up to. You can see: Friends’ Activities: Posts, photos, or updates from the people you have already bonded with. “Friends of Friends” Mentions: Occasional glimpses of second-degree connections (friends of friends) if they’re tagged or co-posting with your direct bond. New Bond Notifications: When two of your friends bond for the first time, or if you form a new bond, it may appear in this feed. Random/Personal Updates: “The tea” or personal shares from your circle. Key Mechanics Discovering Profiles: You can’t directly search for users in We b0nd, but you can tap on a friend-of-friend’s name when they appear here to view their profile. DMs: If you send a message (DM) to a friend-of-friend you haven’t actually met yet, that chat thread looks or behaves slightly differently until you’ve bonded in person. Activity Overflow: Because it’s the largest feed, all sorts of friend-related happenings funnel into it: new bonds, random posts, or updates on group hangouts. Why It’s Special: The Bonds Feed is essentially the “heart” of the app, fostering a sense of community and surfacing interesting interactions within your trusted network and second-degree connections. Bonding (People) Page Purpose and Content A recommendation feed that suggests potential new people (friends-of-friends or similarly aligned users) for you to bond with. You can see: Suggested Connections: People the system thinks you’ll get along with, based on shared friends, location, interests, or prior interactions. Pending Interactions: Users you have already tried to contact (or who reached out to you) appear in a separate section or label, so you know who’s already in progress. Key Mechanics Bonding Cycles: This page has a cooldown timer and refreshes every 3–7 days with new or repeated suggestions. Hiding Users: If you’re not interested in bonding with a particular suggestion, you can hide them (they won’t be re-suggested for the duration of that cycle). Approach vs. Accept: You can send a request (“bond request” or similar) to start a conversation. If they haven’t met you in person yet, there are limitations on how you can interact (see Bonding States below). Why It’s Special: Some We b0nd users will only discover new people via this page instead of real-life meets. The limited refresh or “bonding cycle” encourages timeliness—users must act on suggestions before they’re gone. Engage (Activity and Event) Feed Purpose and Content A feed dedicated to activities and events that your direct bonds—or their friends—are hosting. You can see: Friends’ Activities: Small-scale get-togethers (like going to dinner, playing tennis, day trips) posted by your own circle. Friends-of-Friends’ Activities: If your close friend is attending or co-hosting an activity, it can show up here even if the main host is a second-degree connection. Events by Orgs or Larger Groups: Official parties or bigger gatherings by orgs. Key Mechanics: Attending: You can request to join an activity hosted by a friend-of-friend, even if you’re not directly bonded with them. Activity vs. Event: Activity might be a more intimate group (e.g., tennis with up to 8 people). Event can be a large party or bigger function (e.g., 400-person event). Discovery: Perfect if you’re in a new city and want to find friendly gatherings through mutual connections. Why It’s Special: This feed is the gateway to real-world meetups—extending your network and bridging strangers via mutual friends in a safe, comfortable environment.
